（中央社記者張建中新竹2026年10月30日電）晶圓代工廠力積電 (6770) 大股東力晶 (5346) 預計11月25日召開股東臨時會，討論公司章程修訂，及全面改選董事、監察人。因有股東提名候選人角逐董監事席次，力晶透過公告方式，致全體股東一封信，希望股東能支持董事會提名的人選。

力晶將於11月25日召開股東臨時會，討論公司章程修訂，規劃引進獨立董事及設置審計委員會，完善公司治理架構，並將全面改選董事及監察人，預計選出7席董事及3席監察人。

力晶董事會提名謝明霖、黃崇恆、童貴聰、陳柏霖、黃立德爭取董事，提名鄭素芬和陳錦隆爭取連任監察人，同時提名力積電董事長謝再居和嘉茂交通董事長特助陳鈺婷為董事候選人，提名愛普董事長陳文良為監察人候選人。

力晶股東林緯程等也提名7名董事候選人及3名監察人候選人，爭取董監事席次。力晶經營團隊對此不敢掉以輕心，透過公告方式致全體股東一封信，希望股東能夠支持董事會提名的人選。

力晶在信中表示，力晶集團創辦人暨前董事長黃崇仁今年7月31日逝世，深感哀悼與不捨。黃崇仁多年來帶領團隊深耕半導體產業，以長遠眼光推動企業轉型及投資布局，不僅成就力積電上市，回收晶合集成投資效益，以及分享投資獲利給股東。

力晶指出，黃崇仁2019年推動力晶科技分拆，促使力積電2021年順利上市，成為市值超過新台幣3000億元、台灣第3大晶圓代工公司，力晶持有力積電17.55%股權，除了是最有價值的長期投資資產，也是執行創業投資業務最重要的策略基石。

力晶表示，黃崇仁2015年主導策略投資晶合集成，歷經多年努力，晶合2023年於上海科創板上市，市值達人民幣數百億元；力晶近2年陸續處分部分持股，回收超過百億元資金，大幅提升淨值到新台幣40元以上。

力晶指出，公司於2026年配發每股3.3元現金股利，配發總金額約45億元，將具體投資成果實際回饋全體股東。

力晶表示，為延續黃崇仁推動公司重返興櫃，並朝上市櫃市場邁進的心願，將於11月25日召開股東臨時會，討論公司章程修訂，及全面改選董事、監察人，為下階段的發展奠定基礎，期盼股東能夠支持。

力晶指出，2025年獲利40.3億元，每股盈餘3.01元；2026年上半年獲利約104億元，每股盈餘達7.65元。未來將逐步處分晶合等上市櫃可立即變現的投資標的，適時活化非股票投資資產，提升資金運用效率與獲利能力，期盼公司價值獲得更充分的市場評價。

展望未來，力晶表示，將結合半導體產業優勢、專業人才及策略夥伴資源，掌握AI、半導體與新興科技投資機會，逐步打造專業科技創投平台，並持續強化公司治理與資訊透明度，穩健推進重返資本市場的規劃，為全體股東創造長期價值。

力晶指出，感謝股東長期以來的信任與支持。團隊將珍惜黃崇仁留下的心血，凝聚既有團隊與新世代人才的力量，以實際績效回應股東期待，攜手迎向下一個發展里程碑。（編輯：張良知）

news.Title: 記憶體價格飆升，AI長約鎖單與封測爬坡成為漲勢續航關鍵
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-10-30 08:36:32 數位內容中心 發佈

- 威剛等模組廠獲利暴衝，外資也集中買超華邦電、南亞科等個股，財報與資金同步點燃記憶體族群熱度[1][2]。

- 高毛利AI／伺服器長約優先鎖定供給，加上封測良率與新產能爬坡仍受限，短期現貨與合約市場出現分層與緊張[3][4][5]。

- 這波漲勢能否延伸為中長期趨勢，仍要看原廠長約執行比例、新產能與良率放量速度，以及雲端買家採購節奏與終端廠對價格的承受度[6][7][8]。

2026-10-29，記憶體行情再度成為市場焦點。模組廠威剛公布前三季EPS衝破百元、淨利約336億元，顯示上游漲價已直接反映在模組廠獲利；同日外資集中買超華邦電、南亞科與群聯，單日買超金額分別約42.7億元、25.1億元與21.7億元，也進一步強化市場對供需緊俏延續的押注[1][2]。

財報亮眼、買盤湧入，記憶體股熱度升高

從企業財報可見這波行情的實質影響。旺宏第三季營收242.4億元，季增26.7%、年增195.1%，毛利率達70.5%；公司也將產能由NOR轉向NAND與eMMC，隨著NAND比重提升，營收結構同步改變，反映廠商正透過產能調配追逐更高利潤的產品[9]。市場上也有法人預估，第四季NAND價格可望再漲約30%，DRAM合約價也有雙位數季增空間，進一步帶動資金向記憶體族群集中[7]。

AI長約優先吃下產能，封測與良率成為供給卡點

原廠與大型雲端客戶持續擴大長期供應協議，將可用位元優先配置給AI與伺服器等高階產品，現貨市場可回補的位元因此放緩。多家大廠已與雲端客戶簽下五年甚至更長的合約，部分報導更指出，到2027年將有高比例產能優先供應AI需求[3][10][11]。此外，HBM與先進堆疊產品對封裝、測試要求更高，封測廠雖已調漲報價約2至3成並拉高稼動率，但測試能力與良率仍是限制供給的關鍵。例如大廠報告顯示，HBM4良率年內已由不到60%改善至約80%，說明良率提升能在數月內改變出貨量；只是這類改善多集中在高階產品，對消費級位元的幫助仍有限[4][12][5]。

新產能爬坡同樣需要時間。南亞科指出，新廠將於第1季開始裝機，預計年底投片量達月投片3萬片，目標再擴增至5萬片。這類新增產能屬於逐步放量，短期內對全球位元缺口的緩解仍有限[6]。

雲端客戶拉貨強勁，終端品牌開始承受漲價壓力

需求面則明顯分層，主要由少數超大型雲端客戶主導。隨著庫存快速下降、高密度採購升溫，企業級SSD與高密度DRAM需求同步走強，QLC訂單也被上調，庫存周數從年中約14周降至偏低水位，進一步擴大合約與現貨之間的價差與波動風險[13]。市場上也出現不同聲音：鎧俠執行長警告價格已處高位，且部分供應商已明確把資源轉向AI資料中心市場，顯示業者在公開說法與資源配置上並不一致，也讓後續漲勢多了變數[14][15]。

漲價壓力也開始傳導至終端市場。部分PC品牌已調高旗艦機定價，並調整規格組合以吸收成本；手機廠方面，OPPO表示現有機種暫無調價計畫，但明年新品定價將視記憶體走勢調整，顯示終端廠已將記憶體漲價視為可能延續的成本因素[8][16][17]。

news.Title: STMicroelectronics forecasts higher Q4 revenue on AI chip demand
news.Content:
Investing.com-- STMicroelectronics (EPA:STMPA) forecast higher fourth-quarter revenue on Thursday after reporting a stronger-than-expected recovery in third-quarter sales and margins, supported by improving demand and growth in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The Franco-Italian chipmaker reported third-quarter revenue of $3.76 billion, up 17.9% from a year earlier and above its guidance midpoint of $3.70 billion.

Operating income excluding restructuring and other special items rose 98% to $429 million.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Gross margin increased to 37.3% from 33.2% a year earlier, helped by lower unused-capacity charges and a better product mix.

STMicro forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $4.15 billion at the midpoint, representing sequential growth of 10.5% and a 24.7% increase from a year earlier. It expects gross margin of 39.0%.

The company projected full-year 2026 revenue of about $14.5 billion, up 22.8% from 2025, citing a cyclical recovery across its end markets and growth opportunities in AI data centres and low-Earth-orbit satellite communications.

Chief Executive Jean-Marc Chery said stronger bookings and improving demand visibility supported the recovery, while distribution inventories remained below the company's standard target.

STMicro said it would continue expanding capacity while restructuring its manufacturing footprint and reducing its global cost base to improve profitability.

news.Title: Earnings Preview: What to Expect From Cisco’s Report
news.Content:
Headquartered in San Jose, California, Cisco Systems, Inc. (CSCO) has built a global business around networking, cybersecurity and communications, keeping businesses connected in an increasingly digital world.

With a market cap of nearly $431.8 billion, the company offers network infrastructure, cloud and wireless technologies, data center solutions, collaboration tools, security software, technical support, and managed services, giving it a broad foothold across the technology landscape.

Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today!

The extensive reach sets the stage for Cisco's upcoming Q1 FY2027 earnings report, with Wall Street expecting diluted EPS of $1.15, a 42% increase from the year-ago quarter. Cisco has also beaten EPS estimates in each of the past four quarters, setting a strong precedent ahead of its latest results.

The earnings outlook beyond the current quarter looks equally encouraging, with analysts projecting diluted EPS of $4.42 for full-year FY2027, representing year-over-year (YOY) growth of 21.4%. Analysts also expect the bottom line to reach $8.6 for FY2027, marking a 4.8% increase from the previous year.

The market has already taken notice, sending CSCO stock up 51.9% over the past 52 weeks, far ahead of the S&P 500 Index ($SPX), which gained 12.4%. Cisco has carried that momentum into 2026, with shares advancing 43.2% year-to-date (YTD), compared with a 13.1% rise for the broader benchmark.

Cisco's performance looks even more impressive against the technology sector, where the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) has gained 26.5% over the past 52 weeks and advanced 32.7% YTD. Although those returns reflect a strong run for technology stocks, Cisco has comfortably outpaced the sector.

At the heart of that transformation lies Cisco's push into artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, which has breathed new life into its established networking business. The company reported record Q4 FY2026 revenue of $17.3 billion, up 17.6% YOY, while hyperscaler AI orders reached $4 billion. These orders lifted FY2026 orders to $9.3 billion, roughly 4.5 times the previous year's total.

Story Continues

Cisco's momentum also extends beyond hyperscalers, broadening its market reach. Networking orders climbed 40%, Silicon One chips secured new design wins, and enterprise and sovereign customers continued upgrading their infrastructure. Looking ahead, management expects hyperscaler AI revenue to reach $7.5 billion in FY2027, nearly double this year's roughly $4 billion.

Wall Street's ratings reflect this improving outlook, with the 27 analysts covering Cisco arriving at an overall "Moderate Buy" rating. 16 analysts recommend a "Strong Buy," one assigns a "Moderate Buy," and 10 rate the stock "Hold."

Price targets provide another measure of Wall Street's expectations, with the average target of $133.08 indicating potential upside of 20.7%. Meanwhile, the Street-High target of $165 points to a possible gain of 49.6% from current levels.

news.Title: KLA (KLAC) Q1 2027 Earnings Call Transcript
news.Content:
Image source: The Motley Fool.

DATE

Wed, Oct. 28, 2026

CALL PARTICIPANTS

Vice President of Investor Relations and Market Analytics - Kevin Kessel

Chief Executive Officer - Rick Wallace

Chief Financial Officer - Bren D. Higgins

Full Conference Call Transcript

Operator: Thank you for your continued patience. Your meeting will begin shortly. If you need assistance at any time, please press 0 and a member of our team will be happy to help you. Good afternoon. My name is Stephanie, and I will be your conference operator today. At this time, I would like to welcome everyone to the KLA Corporation September Quarter 26 Earnings Conference Call and Webcast. All participant lines have been placed in a listen only mode to prevent any background noise. After the speakers' remarks, there will be a question and answer session. Thank you. I will now turn the call over to Kevin Kessel, Vice President of Investor Relations and Market Analytics. Please go ahead.

Kevin Kessel: Welcome to the September 26 quarterly earnings call. Joining me are our CEO, Rick Wallace; and our CFO, Bren D. Higgins. We will discuss today's results as well as our outlook. Which we released after the market closed it is available on our website. Along with supplemental materials. We are presenting today's discussion and metrics on a non GAAP financial basis unless otherwise specified. All full year references we make always refer to calendar years. The earnings material contains a detailed reconciliation of GAAP to non GAAP results. Our comments today are subject to risks and uncertainties. Uncertainties reflected in the disclosure of the risk factors in our SEC filings.

Any forward looking statements, including those we make on the call today, are also subject to those risks. And KLA cannot guarantee those forward looking statements will come through. Our actual results may differ significantly from those projected in our forward looking statements. For any subsequent updates, please refer to KLA's IR website which also contains investor events, presentations, corporate governance information and links to our SEC filings. We will begin the call with Rick providing commentary on the quarter and our overall business environment. Followed by Bren, with financial highlights and our outlook. I will pass the call now to Rick. Rick?

Richard Wallace: Thanks, Kevin. KLA's September quarter beat the midpoint of our guidance ranges, across all key metrics. Revenue was another record at $4.14 billion This, coupled with our December quarter revenue guidance of approximately $4.7 billion demonstrates the growth acceleration we plan for the second half of 26. KLA's performance in the quarter was supported by continued strength in leading edge foundry logic related to AI infrastructure investments, and increasing process control intensity across leading edge devices and advanced packaging. Other highlights for the quarter include KLA delivering operating margins above 46% for the first time ever.

Story Continues

Gross margin was 62.7%, and free cash flow was $1.34 billion Over the course of calendar 2026, the AI demand environment has continued to strengthen as reflected in our performance. Additionally, our strong customer engagement has provided visibility into a more favorable outlook for wafer equipment investment for calendar 2026 and 2027. We see this reflected in our growing backlog and sales funnel forecast. We expect momentum across our business to continue into the December quarter, and we are positioned to deliver significant growth in calendar 2027. We have been proactively working with our strategic supply chain partners over the past year to increase their capacity in order to keep up with our demand.

Advanced packaging remains increasingly critical to AI infrastructure expansion. And advanced packaging roadmaps continue to incorporate more wafer front end process, which drive additional process control requirements, KLA's leading process control portfolio enables the company to address these requirements across a growing range of applications. For calendar 2026, Advanced Packaging Process Control Systems revenue remains on track to hit $1.1 billion or more than 70% year over year growth. Nearly twice the growth rate of the advanced packaging market. The growing complexity of KLA's installed base and lengthening tool life cycles continues to increase demand for services.

KLA services revenue was $850 million in the quarter, up 14% year over year supported by a growing installed base and continued customer focus on tool performance, productivity, and availability in this tight system utilization environment. Finally, KLA's process, PCB, and component inspection businesses are also benefiting from technology transitions and the rigorous performance requirements of high performance computing. In summary, KLA is experiencing strengthening momentum driven by growth across the semiconductor ecosystem. Pace of our backlog growth is a key signal of accelerating momentum and provides confidence in our visibility into calendar 2027. Our September quarter results demonstrate the strength KLA's market position and operating model execution. Semiconductors continue to play an increasingly important role across global industries.

With growth driven by investment in AI infrastructure and expanded demand across a broader range of applications and end markets. Together, these trends are supporting stronger, more durable, and more diversified long term growth for the industry. Additionally, the growing complexity of AI enabled semiconductors is increasing process control intensity throughout the manufacturing flow. Reinforcing KLA's long term growth opportunity. KLA's differentiated portfolio is uniquely positioned to address these requirements. While sustained AI data center investment and broader adoption of advanced packaging architectures continue to expand the company's addressable market. As we look ahead, we remain focused on supporting customer roadmaps, investing in innovation and scaling our global capabilities to meet expected demand growth through calendar 2027.

As we progress toward our 2030 target model, we remain committed to disciplined execution, technology leadership, and our proven capital allocation strategy, which will allow us to create durable shareholder value. With that, I will turn the call over to Bren to discuss the quarter's financial highlights.

Bren D. Higgins: Thank you, Rick. KLA delivered strong sequential and year over year growth in the September quarter. For the first time in our company history, KLA delivered operating margins of over 46%. These results reflect our market leadership and disciplined execution. Supported by our global team's dedication and focus on customer success. Revenue of $4.14 billion was above the midpoint of guidance and rose 13% sequentially and 29% year over year. Non GAAP diluted EPS was $1.22 and GAAP diluted EPS was $1.18 each above the midpoint of the respective guidance ranges. Gross margin was 62.7%, slightly above the midpoint of the guidance range. Operating expenses were $688 million including $395 million in R&D, and $293 million in SG&A.

Operating margin rose 240 basis points sequentially to 46.1%. Net income was 1.6 billion GAAP net income was 1.55 billion Cash flow from operations was 1.53 billion and free cash flow was $1.34 billion The company had 1.31 billion diluted weighted average shares outstanding. For the quarter, a breakdown of revenue by reportable segments and markets, major products, and regions, can be found within the shareholder letter and slides. Moving to the balance sheet. KLA ended the quarter with $4.7 billion in total cash equivalents and marketable securities, and $5.95 billion of debt. The company maintains a flexible and attractive bond maturity profile supported by investment grade ratings from all 3 major rating agencies.

The industry outlook continues to strengthen, with visibility improving as customers increase long term investment plans. Despite these fast pace limitations, customers have been very resourceful and are accelerating delivery expectations across all segments. We are therefore raising our expectation for the wafer equipment market including advanced packaging, to approximately the mid-$150 billion range in calendar 2026. KLA backlog continues to grow, and our sales funnel visibility is unprecedented. Supported by new fab investments by a broad base of customers. We continue to plan for significant growth in calendar 2027.

While we will have more to say about market and customer segment expectations for next year in our earnings call in late January, We currently expect the wafer equipment market to exceed $200 billion in calendar 2027. Customer engagement remains robust with numerous new fab projects and greenfield facilities. Scheduled to come online in the quarters ahead. The primary area of focus for our customers is on delivery urgency aligned with new project plans. Against this backdrop, KLA's business momentum and critical role in leading edge process control positions us to deliver accelerating growth for the remainder of calendar 2026 and continuing into 2027.

Our expectations of revenue growth acceleration in the second half of 26 are playing out as more capacity comes online in our long lead time supply chain areas. This is resulting in growth in the second half of calendar year 26 over the first half of approximately 25%. And positions the company for continued sequential growth into calendar 2027. KLA's December quarter guidance is for revenue of $4.7 billion plus or minus $200 million Foundry/logic revenue for semiconductor customers is forecasted to be approximately 60% and memory is expected to be about 40% of semiconductor process control systems revenue to semiconductor customers. Within memory, DRAM is expected to account for approximately 84% with NAND representing the remaining 16%.

As a reminder, these business mix approximations pertain solely to our semiconductor customers and do not fully reflect our total semiconductor process control systems revenue. Gross margin for the December quarter is forecasted to be 62.5% plus or minus 1 percentage point. While the company is demonstrating expected operating leverage across the business as it grows, This is being offset by persistently high memory costs for our system image processing requirements as we have discussed in prior quarters. We are actively engaged across the portfolio to optimize memory efficiency in our systems. Along with other product cost reduction initiatives. These efforts coupled with driving our usual returns based value sharing with our customers, should offset this headwind over time.

Chris Caso: Got it. that is a helpful clarification. Thank you. As my follow-up, I will ask about China. And it looked like it was up significantly in the quarter. I know that revenue tends to be lumpy. Can you talk about what your expectations are for China? what is embedded in the Q4 guidance? And what your thoughts are for the China business as you head into next year?

Bren D. Higgins: Yes. It will come down in Q4 As I said, actually, I think I have been saying this since Mary is I thought that China as a percent of the total would be in the high 20s percentile. So, we will call it somewhere between 27% to 29% And I still believe that, that therefore implies that the fourth quarter is in that similar range given what we have done in the previous 3 quarters. So it did pop up a little bit in September. But China is growing at a much slower rate than the overall business. And so it is coming down as a percent. And I think in 2027, that will continue.

I expect China will likely grow a little bit, but not at the same rate as the growth in wafer equipment outside of China. So we are probably operating somewhere, I would say, in the low 20s percentile in 2027. Now within our numbers, there is also our non semi PC that also has business in China. There is more PCB type investment that happens in China, component inspection in China. So probably skews the numbers a bit up a little bit, but it is a small percentage of the overall, so not much. So I think the numbers I provided give you I think, enough directional clarity about where the business is today and where it is going.

Kevin Kessel: Operator, can you take the next question, please?

Operator: We will go next to Shane Brett with Morgan Stanley. Your line is open.

Shane Brett: The first question is on advanced packaging. At your Investor Day, you mentioned that Cronos is the workhorse of packaging. We have the next 3 systems already ready. Are your customers requiring higher sensitivity tools And if so, can you talk about the competitive environment at these higher sensitivity levels?

Bren D. Higgins: Well, in advanced packaging, it is been flexing because of the move to more front-end-like processes. Most of it, to your point, has been in the macro products And we think the roadmap for those products, we are well positioned there. You are seeing more hybrid bonding and logic devices, which is driving the need for greater levels of sensitivity. We also talked about that at Investor Day. So you start to move from micron level sensitivity down to the 100 nanometer type sensitivity. It does drive the need for more advanced systems. So when we talk about our overall packaging exposure, the mix of systems is starting to trend more towards higher end systems.

So the macro products are still to use your word, the workhorse, but we are seeing more laser scanning and even in some cases, some Gen4 deployment in for packaging requirements. So we think this part of the market continues to be an opportunity for KLA. We have been able to leverage a lot of the R and D that we have done. Across the more advanced platforms. And so we think we are very well positioned with proven products that can meet the higher end requirements. And our customers understand that capability well. So we think we are pretty well positioned in terms of the growth opportunities in that part of the market.

Shane Brett: Got it. Thank you. And my follow-up is on logic, I know you assess node to node share gain after certain wafer start volumes installed. Internally, is there a preliminary expectation on your share gains from 2-nanometer and 1.4 nanometer are there any part of your product portfolio where you think the financial market would be surprised on just the magnitude of share gains?

Bren D. Higgins: Yes. We think the trend is in the right direction. I mean, the thing about the next generation nodes is they are starting to tune those nodes for high performance compute requirements. And those required some of the more advanced capabilities and more sampling steps because of the value of the dye. So with high performance computing, you have large die. They are very valuable. Defect density is a challenge. Also have a very rich design environment. All those are good contributing factors. I do not have a point position to give you in terms of the directional trend, but we feel pretty good about the ability to continue to grow our share of the market node to node.

And I think our relevancy with e beam inspection capability and the linkage we have to our optical becomes more pronounced, And so not as much share as it is adoption. But those investments were made to really they will show up more as we go to smaller designs.

Shane Brett: Got it. Shane you very much.

Operator: And we will take our final question from Timothy Scholes Malander with Rothschild and Company, Redburn. Please go ahead.

Timm Schulze-Melander: Yes. Hi, there. Thanks for taking my questions. 1 for Rick and 1 for Bren. Maybe the first 1, just comparing 2027 to 2026. When you look at the CapEx, that was spent on it or is being spent on established nodes, this year as a percent of the total market and you look forward to 2027, could you just maybe describe how that ratio changes? And then I had a follow-up.

Bren D. Higgins: We have seen more investment in 2-nanometer. I mean, look, I think, 2 nanometer and 3-nanometer investments will be the focus in logic. You will see more there. You will also see some investment in the next generation node, so 1.4 So it is different. You did not have any of that, that more advanced investment, and it was more 3-nanometer centric and 26. So I think it sets up I think, good for us constructively in terms of just more 2-nanometer and more leading edge investment in 1.4.

Timm Schulze-Melander: that is clear. And maybe just thank you. And then maybe 1 on memory in 2027. You have discussed your engineering strategy. About how you are going to address that memory kind of impact to your bill of materials. Can you just maybe talk about what you are purchasing strategy is for 2027, from memory, please?

Bren D. Higgins: Well, certainly, our focus early on and through this year has been mostly around securing supply. When things started to ramp in early 26, we felt pretty good about ensuring we had the supply which was no easy feat generally because of the constraints in the overall industry. And as demand has strengthened, we have had to go out and buy more at higher prices. Less concerned about supply. But certainly, we are exposed to the pricing market. And that is informing the commentary that we provided. But I think from a supply point of view, we feel pretty good about the supply we have secured to meet the requirements we have going forward.

Operator: This does conclude our question and answer session. I would like to turn the program back over to Kevin Kessel for any closing remarks.

Kevin Kessel: Yes. Thank you. Thank you, everyone, again for your interest in KLA. We know it is a very busy earnings day, busy earnings so we appreciate it. If we could not get to your questions, hopefully, we can connect here after the call in our callbacks. And with that, turn it back to the operator to formally close-up the call.

Operator: Thank you. This concludes the KLA Corporation's September quarter 26 earnings call and webcast. Please disconnect your line at this time, and have a wonderful day. Goodbye.

news.Title: KLA Corp (KLAC) (Q1 2027) Earnings Call Highlights: Record $4. ...
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Revenue: Record $4.14 billion, up 13% sequentially and 29% year-over-year; above midpoint of guidance.

December Quarter Revenue Guidance: Approximately $4.7 billion, plus or minus $200 million.

Gross Margin: 62.7%, slightly above midpoint of guidance range.

December Quarter Gross Margin Guidance: 62.5%, plus or minus 1 percentage point.

Operating Margin: 46.1%, up 240 basis points sequentially; first time above 46% in company history.

Operating Expenses: $688 million, including $395 million R&D and $293 million SG&A December quarter guidance approximately $710 million.

Non-GAAP Diluted EPS: $1.22, above midpoint of guidance; December quarter guidance $1.44 plus or minus $0.11.

GAAP Diluted EPS: $1.18, above midpoint of guidance; December quarter guidance $1.41 plus or minus $0.11.

Net Income: $1.60 billion non-GAAP; $1.55 billion GAAP.

Cash Flow from Operations: $1.53 billion.

Free Cash Flow: $1.34 billion.

Services Revenue: $850 million, up 14% year-over-year.

Advanced Packaging Process Control Systems Revenue: On track for approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, more than 70% year-over-year growth.

December Quarter Segment Mix (Semiconductor Process Control Systems to Semiconductor Customers): Foundry logic approximately 60%; memory approximately 40% (DRAM ~84%, NAND ~16% of memory).

Balance Sheet: $4.7 billion in total cash equivalents and marketable securities; $5.95 billion of debt.

Diluted Weighted Average Shares: 1.311 billion for the quarter; December quarter guidance approximately 1.306 billion.

Tax Rate: Planning tax rate of 14.5%.

Other Income and Expense: Net expense of approximately $25 million expected for December quarter.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with MGM.

Is KLAC fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Release Date: October 28, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript .

Positive Points

KLA Corp ( NASDAQ:KLAC ) reported record revenue of $4.14 billion, up 29% year-over-year, and guided December quarter revenue to approximately $4.7 billion, demonstrating accelerating growth.

Operating margin exceeded 46% for the first time in company history, reflecting strong operating leverage and disciplined execution.

Advanced packaging process control revenue is on track to reach approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, growing over 70% year-over-year, nearly twice the market growth rate.

Services revenue grew 14% year-over-year to $850 million, driven by a growing installed base and increasing demand for tool performance and productivity.

KLA Corp ( NASDAQ:KLAC ) expects to outgrow the wafer equipment market in calendar 2027, with a strong backlog and sales funnel visibility, and anticipates the wafer equipment market to exceed $200 billion in 2027.

Story Continues

Negative Points

Gross margin was 62.7%, slightly above the midpoint, but persistently high memory costs for system image processing continue to pressure margins.

Supply chain constraints, particularly for long lead time optical components, have limited KLA Corp ( NASDAQ:KLAC )'s ability to fully meet demand, with lead times averaging around 12 months and extending for some products.

China revenue as a percentage of total is expected to decline to the low 20th percentile in 2027, growing at a slower rate than the overall business.

Operating expenses are forecasted to grow sequentially through 2027, which could impact operating margin leverage if revenue growth slows.

The company faces potential delays in customer fab readiness, which could affect equipment delivery schedules and revenue recognition.

Q & A Highlights

Q : With WFE expected to exceed $200 billion in calendar 2027, how confident are you that KLA can outgrow the roughly 30% market growth, and how does 2027 shape up? A : CEO Rick Wallace said the 2027 setup is "very leading-edge-centric," with breadth of leading-edge node investment, greenfield DRAM, HVM dynamics lifting process control intensity, and advanced packaging growing faster than the market. He noted supply is much improved after 12 months of work, though he is "still behind in supply," with the trajectory nonetheless supporting guidance.

Q : Will 2027 be more linear or back-half loaded, given the strong second-half 2026 ramp? A : CEO Rick Wallace said backlog growth and funnel visibility imply sequential growth for the next several quarters, which suggests a stronger second half, but he expects 2027 to be "more linear" than 2026, without the same significant half-to-half uptick.

Q : Given memory and other cost headwinds, can gross margin return to the 63%+ range in 2027? A : CEO Rick Wallace said the 63%64% target range remains the goal, but advanced packaging and non-semi PC growth are a mix headwind, offset by scale and value-based pricing on new capabilities. He expects improvement as the company moves through 2027, particularly in the middle-to-back half and into 2028, consistent with the March Investor Day model.

Q : When could process control gross margin, which was above 65% in June 2025, return to the mid-60s as DRAM contracts roll off? A : CFO Bren Higgins said on a consistent mix he can see it trending back there in the second half of 2027, since it is difficult to raise prices on existing backlog but new product deals should help. CEO Rick Wallace added that engineering work to use less memory in systems will lower memory content over time, though it takes time to implement.

Q : What are you seeing on lead times, and how are you preparing hiring and the supply chain for a multi-year growth cycle? A : CFO Bren Higgins said lead times average around 12 months, with some products such as Gen4 and Gen5 extending further. KLA is adding headcount in manufacturing, service, applications and engineering, and investing in every factory and with key suppliers, particularly in long lead-time optics, to support a multi-year investment cycle.

Q : Will KLA gain WFE share in 2027 given 12-plus month lead times and low-to-mid-30s market growth? A : CFO Bren Higgins said 2026's first-half weakness was a supply issue rather than demand, and the company remains short on supply today. He feels good about maintaining and growing KLA's relevant share, noting the inflecting parts of the market uniquely benefit process control. CEO Rick Wallace added, "We think we can outgrow next year."

Q : DRAM systems revenue is stepping up sharply in December is this driven by new fabs or rising inspection intensity? A : CEO Rick Wallace said intensity is definitely rising as customers appreciate the incremental value of yield on advanced devices with higher performance requirements. CFO Bren Higgins added that greenfield fabs are driving retooling, yield is "equivalent to printing money," and HBM, I/O counts and logic base die requirements are pushing DRAM intensity in some products toward leading-edge logic levels. Memory is expected to be about 60% of the business in 2027.

Q : How high can WFE grow, and is $300 billion a plausible peak? A : CFO Bren Higgins said the Investor Day view of $220 billion plus or minus $20 billion for 2030 now "looks like a very conservative one," and KLA is more optimistic about higher industry investment levels. The company is having deep conversations with key suppliers about 2029 and 2030 needs to support higher-end scenarios.

Q : Why shouldn't the 2030 model revenue be achievable in 2027 given current WFE levels? A : CFO Bren Higgins said the model assumed service growth tied to installed base expansion, non-semi PC growth, and a few points of semi process control share gain lifting overall share from about 7.5% of wafer equipment in 2025 toward 9%. Those assumptions are not yet met, but he sees no reason the financial model would not perform as laid out as growth comes from the same customers for the same products.

Q : Is the 40%50% incremental operating margin range structurally higher given current performance? A : CFO Bren Higgins said it depends on growth rates: in a normalized environment KLA performs near the midpoint, but with roughly 25% revenue growth it is slightly above the top end, and he expects to be beyond that in 2030. At company growth rates closer to 20%, he would expect performance at the top end of the model or better.

Q : What drove the record CapEx this quarter, and how should we think about CapEx and services growth going forward? A : CFO Bren Higgins said a significant land purchase in India for a new campus drove the quarter. He expects CapEx of roughly 2%3% of revenue, trending to $600$800 million per year as KLA invests at every site. On services, he sees no reason it would not operate at the high end of the long-term growth range in 2027 given installed base growth and high utilization.

Q : Where is KLA in expanding supply, and could December guidance or the $200 billion WFE view have been higher with more supply? A : CFO Bren Higgins said optical components remain the longest lead-time constraint, but KLA does not compete with rivals for its key components, making supply relatively reliable once scheduled. He acknowledged he could have shipped more this year as demand outpaced supply, but incremental supply is coming online month by month. CEO Rick Wallace added that some customers are delaying tool deliveries because their fabs are not ready.

news.Title: 【Hot台股】南亞科漲逾4%後翻黑！網喊「記憶體剩牙科苦撐」分析師示警上檔有壓力
news.Content:
今日社群台股最Hot議題

「牙科優惠時間結束，10點開拉」、「牙科剛綠的是要載人上車？」、「記憶體剩牙科，苦苦支撐」、「昨天沒買到牙科，悶啊」、「牙科重返500大關了嗎」。

「牙科華崩還撐著欸，太扯」、「牙科這波要破前高嗎」、「誰要便宜的牙科？現在大特價給你啊，還不進場看牙」。

針對網友熱議話題…專家這麼說！

HOT台股今日值班專家－啟發投顧分析師白易弘

記憶體大廠南亞科（2408）今（29）日股價震盪，早盤一度衝上497.5元，漲逾4%，距離500元大關僅差2.5元。隨後翻黑又拉回紅盤，不少股民喊「牙科優惠時間結束，10點開拉」，也有股民表示「記憶體剩牙科苦撐」。

白易弘表示，受到昨晚美股科技及記憶體相關族群收高帶動，南亞科今日早盤開高，但由於股價短線已連續上漲，來到480元至500元附近，正好面臨先前高檔套牢區的賣壓，因此開高後漲幅收斂，盤中一度翻黑。

白易弘指出，南亞科近期漲勢較快，短線出現獲利了結賣壓並不意外，若股價拉回至5日均線附近，支撐可能相對較強。他認為，對於尚未進場的投資人，目前不宜急著追高，可先觀察股價是否回落至440元至450元附近，再評估進場時機。

至於網友關注南亞科能否再攻前高，白易弘認為，目前仍有一定壓力，短線須先站穩500元，才有機會進一步挑戰高點。他指出，下周記憶體廠將陸續公布營收，若營運數據提供支撐，南亞科才比較有機會再度挑戰500元關卡。

湯暖萱／財經特派記者，主跑主計處、營建、百貨紡織等

news.Title: 聯電法說變法會「股價打跌停」 智原連拉2漲停
news.Content:
聯電（2303）28日公布第3季財報，營收創單季歷史次高、晶圓出貨量刷新紀錄，還預告2027年平均售價有望成長約10％，並追加32億美元，要布局先進封裝與矽光子。怎料「法說變法會」29日股價開低走低，股價一度打跌停。另一方面，集團旗下智原（3035）股價延續強勢，連拉2根漲停。

第3季營收742億元

聯電第3季合併營收達742.4億元，季增8％、年增25.6％，創單季歷史次高；毛利率34％，營業利益186.4億元，季增24.7％，歸屬母公司淨利164.3億元，每股純益（EPS）1.32元。第3季晶圓出貨量季增7.3％，突破120萬片12吋約當晶圓，創下歷史新高，產能利用率也從第2季的85％提升至92％，部分12吋晶圓廠產能已滿載，8吋晶圓廠營運亦明顯復甦。

展望第4季，聯電預估晶圓出貨量季增1％至3％，美元計價平均售價維持穩健，毛利率約34％，產能利用率則可望維持在91％至93％。執行長王石指出，高階智慧手機、工業應用需求強勁，車用市場也持續復甦，但電腦市場需求相對疲軟。隨著AI基礎建設持續發展，電源管理晶片（PMIC）、現場可程式化邏輯陣列（FPGA）及連接應用需求可望成長。

明年ASP喊漲1成

聯電看好2027年晶圓代工定價環境改善，預期平均售價將較2026年成長約10％，並從明年第1季開始呈現正向成長。然而，財務長劉啟東坦言，晶圓報價調升不代表毛利率就能同步大幅改善，因為原物料成本也在增加，加上未來數年折舊費用將持續上升，預期2027年折舊費用至少呈低個位數成長，2028年增幅可能進一步擴大。

聯電指出，未來至少3年，折舊與原物料成本都將對毛利率形成壓力，即使平均售價上漲，毛利率仍不容易回到過去景氣高峰水準。這也成為市場評估聯電後續獲利的重要變數，投資人關注漲價效益能否抵銷成本增加，以及產能受限後，營收與獲利還能有多少成長空間。

聯電重挫、智原連2根漲停

儘管營運展望不乏亮點，聯電股價仍遭賣壓襲擊。29日盤中最低殺到跌停價115.5元。相較之下，集團旗下智原受惠明年AI營收可望大幅成長，以及成功接獲美系雲端AI應用之大型專案，採用2奈米GAA製程，股價延續強勢，已連續第2個交易日攻上漲停，來到231.5元。

news.Title: 華東Q4營收看續增  毛利率估穩健
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-10-29 09:36:14 王怡茹 發佈

記憶體封測廠華東(8110)受惠記憶體封測需求維持高檔，加上價格調漲效益持續發酵，第三季營收22.63億元，季增16.5%、年增20.9%，創2023年以來單季新高。展望第四季，法人表示，隨主要客戶訂單需求持強，加上封測漲價效益持續挹注，預期營收可望續呈季增，明年展望亦樂觀。

華東隸屬華新麗華(1605)集團，營運以記憶體IC封裝及測試為主，為全球主要記憶體封測業者之一，主力產品為利基型DRAM封測，客戶包括南亞科(2408)、華邦電(2344)等。公司近年持續提高集團企業客戶業務比重，其中華邦電為重要客戶，亦為近年營運成長動能之一。

從營收走勢來看，華東今年7月營收6.88億元，8月進一步攀升至7.98億元，創47個月新高，9月營收則為7.77億元、月減2.66%、年增19.11%；第三季合併營收22.63億元，季增16.5%、年增20.9%，創2023年以來單季新高。累計前三季營收61.76億元、年增15.98%。

獲利方面，華東今年上半年毛利率9.57%，較去年同期轉正；營益率2.74%，亦較去年同期轉正，歸屬母公司稅後淨利13.29億元，每股稅後盈餘(EPS)2.59元，上半年獲利已超越去年全年。

法人分析，隨上游記憶體原廠產能維持高檔，後段封測供需持續緊俏，封測協力廠今年初已陸續啟動漲價，幅度約2至3成，帶動華東毛利率明顯改善。隨主要客戶訂單需求維持強勁，加上價格調整效益持續挹注，預期公司第四季營收有機會較第三季成長，毛利率則有望維持10%左右水準。

此外，華邦電日前宣布，將以全現金方式取得英飛凌(Infineon Technologies)旗下NOR Flash及F-RAM相關事業重組後100%股權，交易預計2027年下半年完成。法人認為，隨主要客戶持續擴大記憶體事業布局，中長期有利華東爭取更多封測委外商機。

news.Title: 【股市焦點】南亞科441元貴不貴？新光證券：供給變化成關鍵
news.Content:
記憶體景氣強勢復甦，南亞科(2408-TW)第3季獲利同步衝上高峰，但股價已提前出現修正，市場開始關注這波DRAM漲價行情還能延續多久。

南亞科第3季營收達1,336.49億元，毛利率85.7%、營益率80%，單季每股稅後純益（EPS）25.4元，稅後淨利876.27億元。第3季DRAM ASP季增逾60%，即使位元出貨量季減中個位數，營收仍較第2季成長61.9%，顯示本波獲利主要由價格上漲帶動。公司10月法說也表示，第4季DRAM市場仍處於缺貨狀態，ASP與毛利率仍有續升空間。

新光證券表示，南亞科第3季毛利率達85.7%，反映DRAM平均售價（ASP）大幅上揚、既有產線成本基礎相對低，以及新廠折舊尚未全面進入成本等因素；以股價441元推算，若採5倍峰值獲利本益比，隱含ASP較第3季回落約11%，若採12倍正常化獲利評價，則隱含ASP下跌約52%，顯示市場已開始交易未來景氣正常化的風險。

延伸市場分析，開始配置你的台美股投資

新光證券指出，股價走勢已開始反映更長期的循環變化。南亞科股價10月初高點一度來到537元，至10月26日最低收在414元，波段回檔約23%，隔日反彈至441元。若直接將第3季EPS年化，全年獲利約101.6元，441元股價對應本益比僅約4.3倍；但新光證券提醒，循環股不能單純以單季高峰獲利年化評價，真正關鍵在於高價能維持多久，以及市場願意給予多少本益比。

新光證券分析，中國長鑫存儲的技術進展也值得留意。長鑫已公布4F² DRAM架構進展，並計畫於年底推出伺服器DDR5 RDIMM，但產品推出仍不等於大規模有效供給，後續仍須觀察客戶認證與良率爬坡。

至於SK海力士，雖然獲利強勁並計畫增加投資，但已與主要客戶簽訂涵蓋2027至2028年逾半產能的長期供貨協議，新增投資是否超過已鎖定需求，同樣是判斷供給壓力的關鍵。

news.Title: KLA Q1 Earnings Call Highlights
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in KLA Corporation? Here are five stocks we like better.

KLA reported record September-quarter revenue of $4.14 billion , up 13% sequentially and 29% year over year, with a company-record 46.1% operating margin and earnings above guidance.

AI infrastructure demand is driving strong growth in leading-edge logic, memory and advanced packaging. KLA expects advanced-packaging process-control revenue to reach approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, up more than 70% year over year.

KLA projected December-quarter revenue of about $4.7 billion and raised its 2026 wafer-equipment market estimate to the mid-$150 billion range, while expecting the market to exceed $200 billion in 2027. China's share of revenue is expected to decline to the low-20% range in 2027.

3 AI Winners, 3 Very Different Paths to Higher Margins

KLA (NASDAQ:KLAC) reported record September-quarter revenue of $4.14 billion, exceeding the midpoint of its guidance range as demand for process-control equipment remained strong across leading-edge foundry, logic, memory and advanced-packaging applications tied to artificial-intelligence infrastructure.

President and Chief Executive Officer Rick Wallace said revenue rose on continued investment in AI-related semiconductor capacity and growing process-control requirements for advanced devices and packaging. The company also projected December-quarter revenue of approximately $4.7 billion, plus or minus $200 million, signaling an acceleration in growth during the second half of calendar 2026.

→ Comfort Systems Earnings: AI Slowdown or More Growth Ahead?

Bearish Pressure Is Building Around These 3 Stocks

"KLA's performance in the quarter was supported by continued strength in leading-edge foundry logic related to AI infrastructure investments and increasing process control intensity across leading-edge devices and advanced packaging," Wallace said.

September-quarter results

Revenue increased 13% sequentially and 29% year over year to $4.14 billion. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share were $1.22, while GAAP diluted earnings per share were $1.18, both above the midpoint of company guidance.

Gross margin was 62.7%.

Operating margin rose 240 basis points sequentially to a company-record 46.1%.

Non-GAAP operating expenses were $688 million, including $395 million in research and development and $293 million in selling, general and administrative expenses.

Net income was $1.60 billion, while GAAP net income was $1.55 billion.

Cash flow from operations totaled $1.53 billion, and free cash flow was $1.34 billion.

Story Continues

→ A 70% Rally Isn't Chord Energy's Only Selling Point

Analysts Just Raised Price Targets On These 3 Semiconductor Equipment Stocks

KLA ended the quarter with $4.7 billion in cash equivalents and marketable securities and $5.95 billion in debt.

Services revenue reached $850 million, up 14% from a year earlier. Wallace said the increase reflected a larger installed base, more complex systems and customer focus on tool performance, productivity and availability amid high system utilization.

Advanced packaging and AI demand

→ Not All Tech Is Getting Crushed: 5 Names Holding Up Through the AI Sell-Off

The company said advanced packaging is becoming more important to AI infrastructure expansion as packaging roadmaps incorporate more sophisticated wafer-front-end processes. KLA expects revenue from advanced-packaging process-control systems to reach approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, representing growth of more than 70% year over year.

Wallace said that growth rate would be nearly twice the growth rate of the advanced-packaging market. In response to analyst questions, Chief Financial Officer Bren Higgins said KLA expects its packaging business to continue growing faster than the market in 2027, with demand increasingly moving toward higher-sensitivity inspection systems as hybrid bonding and other advanced packaging processes expand.

KLA also expects strong memory-related demand. For the December quarter, foundry and logic are forecast to account for about 60% of Semiconductor Process Control Systems revenue from semiconductor customers, while memory is expected to account for approximately 40%. Within memory, DRAM is expected to represent about 84% and NAND about 16%.

Wallace said process-control intensity is rising in DRAM as customers seek higher yields and meet more stringent performance expectations, particularly for advanced memory products. Higgins added that some DRAM products now have process-control intensity comparable with leading-edge logic, aided by greenfield fab investment and demand for high-bandwidth memory.

Industry outlook and capacity investments

KLA raised its estimate for the calendar 2026 wafer-equipment market, including advanced packaging, to approximately the mid-$150 billion range. Higgins said customers are increasing long-term investment plans despite fab-space limitations and that KLA's sales funnel visibility is "unprecedented," supported by new fab investments from a broad customer base.

For calendar 2027, the company expects the wafer-equipment market to exceed $200 billion. Higgins said KLA anticipates sequential revenue growth over the next several quarters, with a more linear progression than the sharp second-half increase anticipated in 2026.

The company said it has been working with supply-chain partners for the past year to expand capacity, particularly for long-lead-time components such as optics. Higgins said average lead times are about 12 months, with some Gen4 and Gen5 product lines taking longer.

KLA is investing in manufacturing, service, engineering and applications staffing, as well as factory capacity. Higgins said capital expenditures should trend higher over the next several years, estimating annual spending of roughly $600 million to $800 million. He noted that a significant land purchase in India for a new campus was a major contributor to the quarter's capital spending.

Management said supply availability had constrained shipments during the first half of 2026, but incremental capacity is now coming online. Wallace also noted that customers can face their own constraints, including delays in clean-room construction, materials and power availability.

Margins, China and December outlook

KLA forecast December-quarter gross margin of 62.5%, plus or minus 1 percentage point, and operating expenses of approximately $710 million. Higgins said persistently elevated memory costs for system image-processing requirements remain a margin headwind, though the company is working to reduce memory usage in its systems, lower product costs and capture value-based pricing on new capabilities.

For the December quarter, KLA expects non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.44, plus or minus $0.11, and GAAP diluted EPS of $1.41, plus or minus $0.11. The company's forecast assumes approximately 1.306 billion fully diluted shares, other expense of about $25 million and a planning tax rate of 14.5%.

On China, Higgins said the country's revenue contribution is expected to decline as a percentage of total sales despite modest growth in absolute terms. He expects China to represent roughly 27% to 29% of revenue in the fourth quarter and to fall to the low-20% range in calendar 2027, as wafer-equipment spending outside China grows more rapidly.

About KLA (NASDAQ:KLAC)

KLA Corporation (NASDAQ: KLAC) develops process control, inspection and yield management solutions for the semiconductor and other advanced manufacturing industries. Its technologies help manufacturers identify defects, measure critical dimensions and monitor production processes to improve quality, reliability and manufacturing efficiency.

The company's product portfolio includes wafer and reticle inspection systems, metrology and measurement tools, defect review and classification systems, and software for analyzing manufacturing data.

news.Title: Why Arm’s Q2 Earnings Could Spur a Recovery in Its Stock
news.Content:
Arm Holdings (ARM) will release its fiscal 2027 second-quarter earnings on Nov. 4. While profit booking following a significant rally has led to a correction in its stock price, its solid Q2 performance and strong Arm AGI CPU demand could spur a recovery.

Arm continues to see strong customer demand across its business, which indicates solid growth ahead. Moreover, it has signed multiple high-value agreements that will support long-term growth.

More News from Barchart

PLTR Stock Earnings Preview: What to Expect From Palantir's Q3 Report

'U.S Has the Best Healthcare in the World. It's Not Even Close' Says Mark Cuban — But the Problem Is Most Americans Can't Afford It

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

Arm's Q2 Outlook

Arm entered fiscal 2027 on a strong footing, led by solid momentum across its business. Strong demand for ARM-based computing architectures across cloud infrastructure, consumer electronics, automotive systems, and emerging AI applications positions it well to deliver solid growth in Q2 and beyond.

Arm reported first-quarter revenue of $1.29 billion, up 22% year-over-year (YoY). The top line benefited from solid performance in the royalty business. Its royalty revenue increased 22% YoY to $715 million, with cloud AI and data center infrastructure emerging as the primary growth engines. Data center royalty revenue more than doubled from the previous year, supported by the expanding adoption of ARM-based server processors among major hyperscalers.

In addition, the growing deployment of data processing units (DPUs) and SmartNICs is providing another growth source, as Arm technology is incorporated into a broad range of leading data center networking products.

In the consumer segment, Edge AI royalties continued to expand despite weakness in the smartphone market. Higher royalty rates, driven by growing adoption of Armv9 architectures and compute subsystems, helped offset softer smartphone sales and the pressure from elevated memory prices. Physical AI also contributed positively, with continued adoption of ARM-based technologies in advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) and autonomous applications supporting demand across the automotive ecosystem.

Licensing revenue is another key growth driver. License and other revenue reached $574 million, up 23% YoY, reflecting strong customer demand for next-generation architectures and deeper strategic relationships with major technology companies. Arm also secured multiple high-value agreements as existing customers renewed long-term licenses. These arrangements, involving hyperscalers, automotive and robotics companies, and handset manufacturers, strengthen Arm's competitive position.

Story Continues

Demand for Arm's AGI CPU offering is also gaining traction, with reported demand exceeding $2 billion. The addition of customers across the U.S. and China, alongside an expanding overall pipeline, points to strong growth ahead.

Looking ahead, management expects the growth trajectory to remain strong in the second quarter of fiscal 2027. Arm forecasts revenue of $1.38 billion, representing approximately 22% YoY growth. Licensing and other revenue are projected to rise about 30%, while royalty revenue is expected to grow at a low-teens rate.

The earnings outlook is also solid, with management projecting adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $0.47 for Q2, up 21% YoY.

Why ARM Stock Appears Compelling Ahead of Q2

Arm's upcoming Q2 earnings could be a key catalyst for a stock-price recovery, supported by strong customer demand, expanding data center adoption, and growing traction for its AGI CPU offering.

Arm is expected to deliver solid revenue and earnings growth, driven by strength in royalty revenue. Higher licensing revenue and long-term agreements with major technology companies also highlight its solid growth prospects. Moreover, rising adoption of ARM-based architectures across AI infrastructure, automotive systems, and consumer electronics provides multiple avenues for sustained growth.

Although ARM stock still trades at a high valuation, the 49% decline from its 52-week high has eased some of these concerns ahead of the earnings announcement.

Analysts currently have a "Moderate Buy" consensus rating on ARM stock and a mean price target of $292.72.

news.Title: AEIS Rides on Strong Data Center Demand: Can It Outpace KLA & MKS?

The company's expanding relationships with hyperscale customers, growing design-win pipeline and next-generation power technologies are strengthening its competitive position against KLA KLAC and MKS MKSI in the rapidly evolving data center market.

In the second quarter of 2026, Data Center Computing revenues increased 35.2% year over year to $191.5 million, driven by strong hyperscale demand. Advanced Energy expects data center revenues to increase more than 50% in 2026. Accelerating hyperscale investments and the ramp-up of next-generation programs are expected to sustain this momentum.

Advanced Energy's investments in 800-volt power architectures represent another significant growth opportunity. Its modular AC-DC and DC-DC solutions offer approximately 98% efficiency, high power density and reliability. Initial production revenues are expected in late 2027, followed by a more meaningful ramp in 2028. This transition could expand Advanced Energy's power content per rack and create additional long-term revenue opportunities.

The company's expanding portfolio has been noteworthy. AEIS recently introduced three new M-CRPS power supplies offering 3200W and 3600W output capacities for AI data centers, networking and telecommunications applications. The OCP-compliant solutions deliver power densities exceeding 100 W per cubic inch, supporting increasingly demanding AI infrastructure requirements. Featuring advanced cybersecurity capabilities, high efficiency and improved thermal performance, the new products are designed to support next-generation CPU and GPU workloads while simplifying system integration and accelerating deployment.

AEIS's expanding portfolio and strong growth across the data center computing market are expected to boost top-line growth and position it favorably against KLA and MKS. For the third quarter of 2026, Advanced Energy expects revenues of $640 million, plus or minus $20 million.

AEIS Faces Stiff Competition

The company is facing stiff competition from companies like KLA and MKS. Both companies are expanding their footprint in the data center space.

KLAC is benefiting from robust data center demand, driven by accelerating AI infrastructure investments and growing adoption of high-performance computing. Increasing demand for advanced logic chips, high-bandwidth memory and sophisticated semiconductor packaging is driving higher process control intensity, strengthening KLA's growth prospects.

MKS is benefiting from rising AI-related investment across semiconductor and advanced packaging markets, with demand broadening through memory, logic, advanced PCBs, photonics, and chemistry equipment. Strong demand for datacom testing solutions and expanding manufacturing capacity further strengthens MKSI's long-term growth prospects. Year to date (YTD), Vicor shares have outperformed the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector, as well as Monolithic Power Systems, Analog Devices and Texas Instruments. Vicor returned a whopping 93.4% YTD while the broader sector, Monolithic Power Systems, Analog Devices and Texas Instruments have returned 14.9%, 33.7%, 54.3% and 78%, respectively.

Vicor Stock's Price Performance

Vicor is benefiting from increasing demand for high-density power delivery solutions as AI processors require greater power efficiency and higher current density. The company's second-generation Vertical Power Delivery (VPD) technology is emerging as a key growth catalyst. VICR claims that its proprietary all-FPA technology can reduce AI processor power losses by 10-15%, while delivering more than 40 times the current gain of integrated voltage regulators (IVRs) and three times the current density of conventional voltage regulators. These advantages are expected to strengthen Vicor's competitive position as next-generation AI processors become increasingly power-intensive.

The company's expanding royalty business has been a key catalyst. In the third quarter of 2026, royalty revenues surged to $66.6 million from $21.7 million in the year-ago quarter. Vicor secured its first VPD license with a leading AI original equipment manufacturer and received licensing inquiries from two hyperscalers. The company expects royalty revenues of at least $43 million in the fourth quarter, even without additional licensing agreements. Further adoption of its patented technologies could create a growing, high-margin revenue stream, although quarterly royalty collections may remain uneven.

Manufacturing expansion represents another important long-term catalyst for the company. Vicor has acquired two additional sites for ChiP Fab-2 and ChiP Fab-3, potentially increasing total manufacturing capacity to nearly five times that of Fab-1. Initial equipment deployment at Fab-2 is expected in the second quarter of 2027. This expansion should help address production bottlenecks, support rising customer demand and unlock additional revenue opportunities.

Story Continues

VICR Benefits From Strong ATE Business & Balance Sheet

Vicor's growth opportunities also extend beyond AI processors. Strong demand for automatic test equipment (ATE) used in ASIC and memory testing is supporting the company's business, with leading ATE customers generating more than $100 million in annual revenues. VICR is also witnessing opportunities in industrial, aerospace and defense markets, particularly from emerging companies developing autonomous technologies. These diversified growth drivers should reduce dependence on any single application and support sustained demand for the company's power solutions.

Vicor's strong balance sheet further supports its long-term expansion plans. The company ended September 2026 with $513.1 million in cash and cash equivalents. VICR expects to finance Fab-2 and eventually Fab-3 without raising additional capital. Improving operating cash generation and increased production scale should strengthen the company' ability to fund innovation, expand manufacturing and capitalize on emerging growth opportunities.

Vicor's 2026 Earnings Estimate Revision Shows Rising Trend

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings is pegged at $3.94 per share, up 8% over the past 30 days, suggesting 51% growth from the 2025 reported figure.

Vicor Corporation Price and Consensus

Vicor Corporation price-consensus-chart | Vicor Corporation Quote

The consensus mark for fourth-quarter 2026 earnings is pegged at $1.13 per share, down by four cents over the past 30 days and indicating 12% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

Conclusion

Despite its premium valuation and impressive YTD rally, Vicor remains an attractive investment proposition, supported by strong AI-driven demand, expanding royalty revenues and growing adoption of second-generation VPD technology. The company's manufacturing expansion, solid backlog and strong balance sheet further strengthen its long-term growth prospects. Although elevated valuation and near-term capacity constraints remain concerns, VICR's technological leadership and expanding growth opportunities justify its premium and make the stock worth considering for long-term investors.

Vicor currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: Lumentum Shares Jump 135% YTD: Can AI Momentum Sustain the Rally?
news.Content:
Lumentum LITE shares have surged 135% year to date (YTD), outperforming the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's return of 16.5%. The outperformance reflects investor optimism about the company's expanding role in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, accelerating demand for optical connectivity and improving profitability. Strong hyperscaler spending, growing adoption of 1.6T optical transceivers, optical circuit switches (OCS) and next-generation laser technologies are strengthening Lumentum's growth prospects.

These factors have helped LITE shares outperform peers, including Cisco Systems CSCO, Broadcom AVGO, and Coherent COHR YTD. Shares of Coherent and Cisco have returned 27.8% and 45.3%, respectively, while Broadcom shares have dropped 1.1%. Despite robust demand, LITE faces challenges in expanding manufacturing capacity sufficiently to meet customer requirements. Apart from stiff competition, LITE's dependence on a limited number of major customers exposes its business to changes in purchasing patterns and capital spending priorities. So, what should investors do with the LITE stock? Let's find out.

LITE Stock's Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Lumentum Shares Are Overvalued

Lumentum shares are overvalued, as suggested by a Value Score of F.

In terms of the trailing 12-month price/sales, LITE is trading at 10.48X, higher than the broader sector's 5.57X. Lumentum is trading at a higher multiple compared with peers, including Coherent's 3.9X, Cisco's 6X and Broadcom's 9.39X.

LITE's Valuation

LITE Faces Multiple Challenges

Lumentum faces challenges in expanding manufacturing capacity sufficiently to meet customer requirements. Tight availability of laser components and other materials could restrict shipments and delay revenue realization. The company is expanding ultra-high-power laser production across its San Jose, U.K. and Greensboro facilities.

The company suffers from customer concentration. LITE's dependence on a limited number of major customers exposes its business to changes in purchasing patterns and capital spending priorities. Lumentum's two largest end customers accounted for 26.6% and 15% of fiscal 2026 revenues, respectively, representing a combined 41.6%. Moreover, the company's expanding OCS business currently depends heavily on one major customer.

Lumentum faces competition from established optical technology suppliers, including Coherent, Broadcom, InnoLight and Eoptolink. Additionally, the shift toward silicon photonics presents challenges for Lumentum's EML business.

Story Continues

Can Strong AI Opportunity Aid LITE's Prospects?

Lumentum is benefiting from increasing investments in AI data centers, which require high-bandwidth, low-latency optical connectivity. The transition from copper-based connections to optical technologies is creating opportunities across scale-out, scale-across and scale-up networking architectures. Increasing adoption of AI accelerators and larger computing clusters is driving demand for Lumentum's lasers, optical components and transceivers.

The company is benefiting from accelerating adoption of next-generation 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers as hyperscalers upgrade their AI networking infrastructure. Lumentum achieved record 800G shipments and initiated production shipments of 1.6T transceivers during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. Lumentum expects the adoption of 1.6T transceivers to accelerate through calendar 2027, supported by deployments of custom AI clusters among leading hyperscale customers.

Lumentum's OCS business represents a significant growth opportunity as hyperscalers seek energy-efficient networking solutions. OCS technology enables dynamic traffic routing while reducing power consumption and optical signal losses compared with conventional electrical switching. OCS shipments doubled sequentially in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, while the company's first-quarter outlook included its first quarter of more than $100 million in OCS revenues.

LITE's 2027 Earnings Estimate Revision Shows Rising Trend

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $21.40 per share, up 0.5% over the past 30 days, suggesting 146.8% growth from the fiscal 2026 reported figure.

Lumentum Holdings Inc. Price and Consensus

Lumentum Holdings Inc. price-consensus-chart | Lumentum Holdings Inc. Quote

The consensus mark for first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $4.22 per share, unchanged over the past 30 days and indicating 283.64% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

Conclusion

Lumentum's strong exposure to AI infrastructure, accelerating adoption of 1.6T optical transceivers and expanding OCS opportunities bode well for its long-term growth prospects. Upward earnings estimate revisions further reinforce optimism. However, the stock's premium valuation, customer concentration, intense competition and manufacturing capacity constraints warrant caution. Following the sharp YTD rally, much of the growth potential appears priced in, limiting near-term upside. Hence, investors may consider holding LITE shares at current levels rather than chasing the rally, while monitoring execution and profitability improvements.

Lumentum currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: Top 5 AI Stocks in Billionaires Ray Dalio and Philippe Laffont’s Portfolios
news.Content:
Billionaires Ray Dalio and Philippe Laffont are two of the brightest minds in investing, and both have strong views on AI. Laffont runs Coatue Management and has built his hedge fund around the technology. Dalio founded Bridgewater Associates in 1975 and warns that AI has become a crowded trade. Let's start with Laffont.

Laffont: AI Is a Supercycle, and the Next $10 Trillion Company Could Come From It

Laffont sees a supercycle in AI, and Coatue's four biggest US long positions as of March 31 were all AI-related, Bloomberg reported. Coatue's flagship hedge fund lost 8.3% in July, its worst month in more than a year, but was still up 14.3% for the year (at the time of the Bloomberg report), after a gain in May that was its best month in 25 years, Bloomberg said in August. Check his top stock picks here.

Laffont expects a $10 trillion company within 10 to 15 years, he told CNBC in June. He thinks the winner could be a new AI name. There is "a good chance that OpenAI and Anthropic could be there," he said, and SpaceX could join them.

Agentic AI excites him most. Laffont described going to bed while a thousand AI agents do the work, and he says the productivity gains already show up in his own office. He does not expect AI models to become free, because people will pay for the best ones.

Dalio: AI Is a Great Tool and a Crowded Trade

Dalio built Bridgewater out of a two-bedroom apartment, and its flagship Pure Alpha fund rose 33% in 2025, Reuters reported. Click to read more about Dalio's portfolio.

A US debt crisis could hit within three years, he told Bloomberg Television in October. The government spends about 40% more than it takes in, he says, and debt payments squeeze out other spending. Stocks look expensive by most of his measures, and the extra return they offer over bonds has shrunk. AI adds to the risk, because a small group of AI stocks drives the market, and the big AI spenders now rely more on debt to fund their buildout. His one warning to investors is to avoid being "too concentrated in one particular asset," such as AI.

Dalio still likes AI as a tool. Using it to systematize investment decisions is the future, he says, and he expects gains to broaden from the AI builders to the companies that use the technology.

Both billionaires own AI stocks. Here are the 5 biggest AI holdings the two funds have in common. You can see the full list of 10 stocks here .

Methodology

We looked at the top 50 holdings in the second quarter 2026 13F filings of Ray Dalio's Bridgewater Associates and Philippe Laffont's Coatue Management. From the AI stocks that appear in both lists, we picked the 10 with the highest combined dollar value across the two stakes and ranked them in ascending order. Stake sizes and share changes come from the funds' 13F filings for the quarter ended June 30.

Story Continues

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 599.2% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 372 percentage points ( see more details here ).

You can also watch our video about the top 10 AI picks of these two famous billionaires on YouTube by clicking the image below:

#5 GE Vernova Inc. (NYSE:GEV)

Coatue Stake $3.01 Billion | Bridgewater Stake $144.2 Million

GE Vernova makes the gas turbines and grid equipment that data centers need for power. Coatue trimmed 14,194 shares in the second quarter and held $3.01 billion, or 6.18% of its portfolio. Bridgewater trimmed 312,129 shares and held $144.2 million, or 0.59% of its portfolio. Bulls say the company's order backlog for AI data center power outweighs a recent earnings miss. See the full breakdown here.

GE Vernova (NYSE:GEV) is positioned to benefit from surging electricity demand driven by AI data centers. US data center electricity consumption is projected to increase 130% by 2030, creating opportunities across power generation and grid infrastructure. GE Vernova's gas turbine backlog and slot reservations reached 116 gigawatts, while data center orders exceeded $5 billion in the first half of 2026, more than double the total for 2025.

Second-quarter orders surged 88% year over year, lifting the company's total backlog to $176 billion. Its businesses span gas turbines, transformers, substations and electrical equipment, allowing it to benefit from multiple stages of data center development. Growing equipment installations could also generate long-term maintenance and service revenue.

However, not all is good. GE Vernova's valuation already reflects substantial growth expectations. The stock trades at 53.74 times forward non-GAAP earnings, compared with the sector median of 19.32 times. Its forward enterprise value-to-sales ratio of 4.52 is more than double the sector median. These premiums leave limited room for disappointment if AI-related electricity demand grows more slowly than anticipated. Supply chain constraints could also delay the conversion of GE Vernova's substantial backlog into revenue.

#4 Applied Materials, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMAT)

Coatue Stake $3.05 Billion | Bridgewater Stake $210.7 Million

Applied Materials sells the equipment and services that chipmakers use to manufacture semiconductors. Coatue trimmed 1,034,719 shares and held $3.05 billion, or 6.26% of its portfolio. Bridgewater trimmed 268,492 shares and held $210.7 million, or 0.86% of its portfolio. Jim Cramer thinks there is more to the stock than its earnings multiple shows. Check what he said here.

Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) makes the machines chipmakers use to build semiconductors. Without them, Nvidia, Micron and others could not produce the chips AI needs. Chip shortages are expected to last for years, with memory shortages forecast to run through 2030, so chipmakers must keep adding capacity. Cloud giants keep raising their AI spending, and asset managers are building new funds focused on data centers. In the latest quarter, margins and earnings grew faster than sales. The stock has fallen about 48% from its high, and its forward P/E has dropped from about 55 to 29.5, which gives long-term buyers a cheaper entry.

The bull case rests on AI demand lasting for years, and nobody can guarantee that. Some investors expect the boom to end quickly, and chip equipment orders can swing sharply when chipmakers pause spending. The stock is also very volatile, which makes it a poor fit for conservative investors. A valuation recovery, with the forward P/E climbing back toward 40, is not certain, and a lower multiple would cut any gains. A 48% drop can also mean the market sees a problem that the numbers do not yet show at Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT).

#3 Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN)

Coatue Stake $2.82 Billion | Bridgewater Stake $482.8 Million

Coatue raised its Amazon stake by 50% in the second quarter, buying 3,904,033 shares, and held $2.82 billion, or 5.80% of its portfolio. Bridgewater cut 2,363,230 shares, which took the position from 4.08% to 1.98% of its portfolio. The stake is still worth $482.8 million. Amazon also ranks second on our list of President Trump and Nancy Pelosi's top picks. Read why here.

Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) owns huge data centers full of computers and rents them out over the internet through AWS, its cloud business. AI companies need an enormous amount of computing power, so they rent it from Amazon and pay every month, like tenants paying a landlord. AWS growth has sped up for five straight quarters, reaching 37% last quarter, and Amazon says its capacity is sold out through 2027. Customers have signed contracts for years of future use, and that backlog doubled in the first half of the year. Anthropic and OpenAI are two of the biggest tenants, and Amazon owns stakes in both, so it gets paid as their landlord and as an owner. Advertising adds another strong profit stream, up 26% last quarter.

Amazon is spending so much on new data centers that free cash flow has turned negative and its debt has grown. If AI demand slows, those buildings will be expensive to keep. Much of the backlog comes from OpenAI and Anthropic, two companies that spend far more than they earn. A possible Anthropic IPO, which would put a public price on Amazon's stake, could also price below its last funding round. AI shopping agents could skip the sponsored products that drive most of Amazon's ad revenue, and the FTC's antitrust trial starts in March 2027 for Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN).

#2 Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MU)

Coatue Stake $3.63 Billion | Bridgewater Stake $134.7 Million

Micron makes the memory chips that go into data centers and AI servers. Coatue raised its stake by 1,794%, buying 2,976,338 shares, and the position grew from 0.19% to 7.46% of its portfolio. It was worth $3.63 billion at the end of the quarter. Bridgewater went the other way and trimmed 1,359,038 shares, which cut the weight from 2.23% to 0.55% of its portfolio. It held $134.7 million. A Chinese memory maker could match Micron's DRAM wafer capacity by 2029, and that is the core of the bear case. Read the full bear case here.

Micron (NASDAQ:MU) is trading at about 5 times forward earnings, against a sector median of 21.6. Its forward PEG ratio is 0.07, against 1.13 for the sector, and on trailing earnings it trades at 11.6 times, well below its five-year average of 18.3. Revenue grew 256% from a year ago, and earnings have surged with it.

But before you get too excited about the valuation, listen to the bear argument. Bears say a low P/E on record profits is a warning sign for a cyclical stock. They point to Micron's own history, where strong earnings and a low P/E came before a big drop at least three times in the past decade. Fabs cost billions and take two to three years to build, so new supply from SK hynix and Chinese makers will arrive later, as it did after the PC era, the dot-com bubble, the 2017 cloud surge and the pandemic boom. Even bears say the shortage may last into 2028, but they expect the stock to peak before it ends, and Micron is already well below its June high. AI spending cannot grow forever, and the big spenders already have negative cash flow, which is a risk for Micron (NASDAQ:MU).

#1 Lam Research Corporation (NASDAQ:LRCX)

Coatue Stake $4.09 Billion | Bridgewater Stake $406.6 Million

Lam Research makes the machines that chipmakers use to build chips. It is Coatue's second-largest position, at $4.09 billion or 8.41% of its portfolio, after Coatue trimmed 601,902 shares. Bridgewater trimmed 633,005 shares and held $406.6 million, or 1.67% of its portfolio. The stock was up about 73% for the year when we last covered it. Read our take on whether it is still a smart long-term AI pick here.

Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) makes the etching and deposition machines chipmakers use to build wafers. Advanced AI chips need more of those steps and take longer to make, so manufacturers need more equipment even if unit volumes stay the same. Bulls also see Lam as a shelter if the AI market cools. If AI chip prices fall as costs normalize while volumes rise, chipmakers still have to buy the machines to make them. Sales grew 54% last quarter, operating margins reached a record high, and the stock has fallen 29% since June, which gives new buyers a cheaper entry.

Guidance for the next quarter points to just 4.6% growth from the last one, after 22% in the September quarter, because unusually strong China orders are returning to normal. The stock fell about 12% on the report. China's strength may only be a timing issue as chipmakers absorb equipment they already bought, and ASML and Applied Materials both say demand there remains strong. Even so, equipment orders come in lumps, and a real pullback in AI spending would hit Lam directly.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of LRCX as an investment, we believe certain AI infrastructure stocks offer far stronger long-term potential at a much more attractive entry point. If you are looking for an AI stock more promising than LRCX that operates as a critical AI tollbooth and stands as the most important company in the world, check out our report about this must-own AI stock .Click to continue reading and see the expanded list of 10 Stocks Billionaires Laffont and Dalio are Piling Into
